transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-10 | Start: 16:00 PT | Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Theo Ramirez (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Solutions Eng); Lina Chen (Constellation, Head of ML), Ethan Brooks (CTO), Samir Patel (Platform Eng), Rosa Diaz (Security)

Auto-generated summary (auto):
- Goal: Scope POC for Constellation Platform to validate Redwood inference integration using OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling, structured JSON output, and perf/latency/cost benchmarks.
- Key success criteria: end-to-end latency targets, throughput for nightly batch reranks, and security/compliance checks (SOC2, KMS).

[00:00] Maya: alright hey everyone thanks for joining this is Maya from Redwood, um I'm the AE on the account. quick agenda: scoping the POC success metrics, workload sizing, bench—benchmarks, and then integration plan — SDKs and OpenAI-compatible endpoints and function calling.
[00:18] Ethan: thanks Maya, yeah we wanted to make sure we cover the timelines too, we have Q2 landing criteria for this feature so timeline is a little tight.
[00:26] Lina: hi all, quick note — our primary use case is a nightly rerank + an online assist widget for customer success agents, and we want structured JSON output with tool calls for enrichment.
[00:39] Samir: and from infra perspective we care about VPC/private deployment options and KMS key control, also need to know what kind of throughput we can expect during our morning ramp.
[00:51] Theo: perfect. I can run some initial benchmarks; can you confirm current traffic patterns and payload sizes?
[00:58] Lina: sure so the nightly batch is about 10k documents, average seq length after tokenization is ~600 tokens per doc, we do rerank that produces a 3-5 candidate list. Online assist is 150-300 token conversations, 95th percentile request size is ~220 tokens.
[01:18] Jordan: got it. for batching/throughput numbers that's helpful — for the nightly job we usually target throughput more than latency, for the widget it's p99 latency that matters.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing (tokens/doc, concurrency), benchmarks (p99, throughput, cost), timelines, integration plan (SDKs, endpoints, function/tool calling, structured output schema)

[02:05] Maya: let's capture success criteria first, Lina — what are you measuring to call this POC a win?
[02:12] Lina: three things — 1) accuracy parity or better vs current in-house reranker (we'll provide eval set), 2) online latency for the widget under 250ms p99 for 200-token sequences, and 3) cost per 1M tokens not to exceed our budget — ballpark $1200 per 1M tokens for hosted equivalent, but we are flexible if dedicated drops it.
[02:34] Ethan: and from product side we also need structured JSON output for downstream ingestion, schema we can share; and must support tool/function calling to call our enrichment microservice (entity lookup) synchronously.
[02:48] Maya: great, those are clear. Redwood can support tool calling via function-calling style endpoints — we expose an OpenAI-compatible API surface and SDKs, and we can also host dedicated pools with VPC if you want private networking.
[03:05] Rosa: can you explain the KMS / key control story quickly? we need to know if customer-managed keys are possible.
[03:11] Theo: yes — for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations, and we can integrate with AWS KMS for key rotation and logs. For Dedicated customers we offer network isolation and optional KMS. For hosted we encrypt at rest with our keys but we can offer bring-your-own-key in Private. (murmurs)
[03:32] Samir: okay that's helpful. For the POC we'll probably try hosted first and then move to a dedicated pool if perf/cost justify.

[04:00] Maya: timeline — you said Q2 landing, what's your target date?
[04:05] Ethan: end of Q2 would be ideal, so we need the POC complete by mid-May to a deployed pilot by end of June. so POC in ~4 weeks.
[04:16] Maya: tight but doable. we recommend a 3-4 week POC: week 0 onboarding + dataset transfer, week 1 bench + initial integration, week 2 iterate on prompts and model variants, week 3 finalize SLOs and handoff.
[04:30] Lina: ok that's reasonable. what benchmarks will you run?
[04:34] Theo: I'll run two tracks: 1) accuracy baseline — run Redwood's eval harness against your eval set and compare rerank metrics, 2) perf benchmarks — p50/p95/p99 latencies for online flows using the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, as well as throughput for batch rerank (tokens/sec and docs/sec). we'll capture token cost estimates with batching/quantization profiles.
[04:55] Samir: what's your typical p99 on a hosted config for 200-token seq with our model family?
[05:00] Theo: rough ballpark — for a 7B-ish quantized model on our hosted flow you might see ~120–180ms p99 for short sequences, but that depends on concurrency and prefix caching; for 600-token sequences that's higher — p99 can be 700–900ms unless we use dedicated throughput or a model variant optimized for long context.
[05:19] Jordan: also keep in mind continuous KV cache for conversational flows can drop costs and tail latency if you reuse prefixes.

[06:00] Ethan: about the integration — we want to use minimal changes to our codebase, is your API fully OpenAI-compatible?
[06:08] Maya: yes — we have an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and SDKs in Python/Node — examples for completions/chat, streaming, embeddings and function-calling. the plan would be to swap endpoint URLs and update key. we also provide a passthrough that supports the function-calling schema.
[06:24] Lina: any caveats in the mapping? we've had issues where tool-calls weren't consistent across vendors.
[06:29] Theo: there are small differences — e.g., our function-calling requires explicit schema definitions and we return a structured 'tool_call' wrapper in the response; occasionally autogenerated names get mangled in transcription, but the payload is JSON. Jordan will provide a sample SDK snippet that shows the function signature and how to parse the response.
[06:48] Jordan: yes I'll put an example in the repo — small Node example and a Python snippet that shows how to register your enrichment function and handle the sync call.

[07:05] Samir: how do you handle streaming and partial results? our widget wants progressive render.
[07:11] Theo: we support streaming via chunked transfer; for OpenAI-compatible streaming it's the same event format — we stream tokens and also support streaming structured output by delimiting with the functions wrapper. small nuance: when using streaming + function calling you need to wait for the final call payload in some cases. we'll document this in the SDK examples.

[08:00] Rosa: security question: do you provide audit logs of requests + responses? we need to show data access for SOC2 and for our auditors.
[08:08] Maya: yes audit logs are available for Dedicated and Private, and we can provide limited logs for hosted under enterprise agreements. logs include request metadata, route, latency; for body-level logging we can support sampling or redaction.
[08:23] Rosa: and data residency? we need EU storage for EU tenants.
[08:27] Maya: we have region support and can pin the tenant to EU region for data at rest. for Private deployments you obviously control residency.

[09:00] Lina: for structured output we will share a JSON schema for the rerank output (rank, score, matched_entities array) — will the SDK validate or do you expect us to validate?
[09:12] Jordan: Redwood's SDK includes a lightweight schema helper for assertions; we also recommend validating on your side. For POC we'll run a schema-conformance check and include it as part of the accuracy pipeline.

[10:00] Maya: can we go over concrete benchmarks and what you'll provide for the eval?
[10:06] Theo: yes, for perf we'll provide a spreadsheet with columns: model_variant, instance_type, concurrency, seq_length, p50/p95/p99, tokens_per_sec, cost_estimate_per_1M_tokens. for accuracy we'll produce precision@k/ndcg on your eval set and a qualitative set of failure cases.
[10:26] Ethan: we want to see both hosted and dedicated numbers if possible — cost and perf trade-off.
[10:31] Theo: understood. I can spin up a dedicated test pool for the POC but it will need a short commit for reserved capacity — we can do a short-term trial with a temporary dedicated pool, or emulate dedicated on hosted with higher priority. I'll outline pros/cons in the sheet.

[12:00] Lina: sample sizes — how many eval queries do you need for stable metrics?
[12:05] Theo: for rerank we recommend at least 5k labeled queries to stabilize ndcg estimates, but we can start with 1k for an initial signal. for latency p99 you'll want sustained traffic for a few minutes across the concurrency profile to get accurate tails.

[14:00] Samir: IAM integration — we have cross-account roles for S3 access and our infra team wants logging to CloudTrail. can Redwood access S3 with a role?
[14:09] Maya: yes provide a read-only role or pre-signed URLs, both work. For Dedicated/Private we can also use VPC endpoints and VPC peering. For audit logs we can stream to your storage in some cases — we'll capture specifics in the security doc.

[15:00] Ethan: what about model versions and rollouts? we need pinning for reproducibility.
[15:07] Jordan: you can pin model versions per route and we support A/B rollouts and canary percentage traffic. that's part of Redwood Console; we'll show the UI in the demo.

[16:00] Lina: how do you estimate cost for batching? for the nightly job we might pack sequences together.
[16:06] Theo: batching efficiency depends on sequence length variance — for 600-token docs we can get decent packing but there is diminishing returns; we'll measure tokens/sec and effective cost after batching and quantization. quantized 4-bit kernels help reduce GPU compute cost significantly.

[18:00] Rosa: any third-party certs? you mentioned SOC2 earlier — do you have the report?
[18:06] Maya: we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001; I will share redacted reports and our security whitepaper — Jordan will attach these to the follow-up email.

[20:00] Ethan: on timelines, Maya you mentioned week 0 onboarding — what does that include?
[20:07] Maya: onboarding: account creation, API keys, region selection, one-off networking config if needed, and a short KB with SDK examples. For dataset transfer: Samir provides S3 link and we verify access. Then Theo will run bench.

[22:00] Samir: about the SDK snippet — we use TypeScript on the backend, can you provide a minimal example?
[22:07] Jordan: yes, I'll push a TypeScript example showing the OpenAI-compatible request to the repo and a handler for function calling + parsing structured JSON.

[24:00] Maya: ok let's call out explicit success criteria to capture in the SOW: 1) ndcg >= baseline (or specified delta), 2) widget p99 <= 250ms for 200-token seq at 50 concurrent users, 3) nightly rerank throughput process 10k docs within 2 hours, 4) security sign-off (Rosa).
[24:30] Lina: yes add those; for the throughput number 2 hours is flexible but we'd like <3 hours if needed.

[26:00] Theo: small note on measurement: p99 can be noisy; we'll include both p95 and p99 and run repeated runs to smooth results. Also we'll include cold-start profiles.

[28:00] Ethan: about function/tool calling latencies — if the model calls our enrichment microservice synchronously how's end-to-end latency measured?
[28:10] Jordan: it's basically model latency + network call to your service; we recommend hosting the enrichment microservice in same region and keeping the enrichment call fast (sub 50ms ideally). We can also support async tool-calling where the model returns a tool call request and you respond separately, which can help reduce tail latency for the widget.

[30:00] Samir: will you help with local validation — like a small harness to run our dataset against Redwood endpoints?
[30:07] Theo: yes we'll provide a small harness script and the performance spreadsheet. We'll need API key and sample payload shapes.

References shared: "security_whitepaper.pdf" (link in chat), "POC_benchmark_template.xlsx" (shared perf spreadsheet), SDK repo link (private)

[34:00] Maya: risks and trade-offs: hosted is fastest to start but can be more expensive at scale; dedicated reduces unit cost and gives isolation but has higher commitment. Private gives max control but higher integration work. We'll include cost models in the follow-up.

[36:00] Lina: do you support quantization options from our side? we want to test quantized variants.
[36:08] Theo: yes we support multiple quantization profiles; we'll test 4-bit and 8-bit variants in the benchmarks and include quality regressions in the accuracy report.

[38:00] Rosa: last security question — how long do you keep request logs? will there be a retention setting?
[38:08] Maya: yes retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private; for hosted we have defaults but can negotiate retention windows for enterprise.

[40:00] Ethan: ok next steps recap?
[40:05] Maya: I'll read them out — Redwood to send SOW + pricing, Theo to run benchmarks and share spreadsheet, Jordan to push SDK examples and security docs, Samir to provide S3 link, Constellation to confirm timeline. Any other items?
[40:18] Lina: please include a short demo of the console for model pinning and rollouts.
[40:22] Maya: will do.

[44:00] Closing: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the security review and bench kickoff.
